annotation.title_clean: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1110 amending Regulation (EU) No 748/2012 as regards the initial airworthiness of unmanned aircraft systems subject to certification and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/947 as regards the rules and procedures for the operation of unmanned aircraft
annotation.title_en: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1110 amending Regulation (EU) No 748/2012 as regards the initial airworthiness of unmanned aircraft systems subject to certification and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/947 as regards the rules and procedures for the operation of unmanned aircraft
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Commission implementing regulation setting initial airworthiness rules for certified unmanned aircraft systems operated in the 'specific' category. It amends Part 21 of Regulation 748/2012 and Regulation 2019/947, requiring airworthiness and noise certificates, incident reporting to design holders and compliance with mandatory safety information. Applies from 1 May 2025.
key_provisions_or_claims: Operators of certified UAS in the 'specific' category must hold a certificate of airworthiness or restricted certificate, plus a noise certificate where applicable.
Operational authorisation requires valid airworthiness certificates or approved flight conditions.
Operators must report safety-related events, accidents and serious incidents to the design approval holder.
EASA's safety and information-security analysis systems extend to control and monitoring units and components.
Applies from 1 May 2025; certain information-security provisions apply from 22 February 2026.
